_description: These ratios are P(observation|state) values relative to a neutral baseline (1.0).
They are used by operate.py bayesian_update() to update BeliefState each iteration.
CALIBRATION INSTRUCTIONS:
1. Collect a labeled dataset of (screen_observation, true_state) pairs from
production runs. Log perception snapshots alongside ground-truth state tags.
2. For each state category, count how often that category was active when the
true world state matched (e.g., app:firefox active when Firefox was focused).
3. Normalize each count relative to the neutral baseline frequency to produce
P(observation|state) / P(observation|neutral).
4. Replace the values below with your empirical ratios.
5. Validate: ratios > 1.0 mean 'this observation is MORE likely under this state'.
Ratios < 1.0 mean 'this observation is LESS likely under this state'.
DEFAULT VALUES (developer heuristics — replace with empirical measurements):
app_match_with_delta=0.95 : App focused + world changed = strong positive evidence
app_match_no_delta=0.75   : App focused + world stable  = moderate positive evidence
ui_rich=1.50              : Many UI entities            = environment is active/busy
ui_sparse=1.20            : Few UI entities             = environment partially busy
ui_empty=0.80             : No UI entities              = mild negative evidence
neutral_with_delta=1.00   : Fresh observation           = no update to prior
neutral_no_delta=0.80     : Stale observation           = mild negative evidence
ENTITY_RICH_THRESHOLD=10  : Entity count above which ui_rich fires (integer)
